statement: >= 20% of announced >100 MW AI data-centre capacity is outside the two leading jurisdictions (Epoch data-centre tracker; IEA; 2027)
status_at_phase_end: No in-phase series for >100 MW AI-specific capacity (data-gap for the named series). Best proxy publicly known in 2023: hyperscale capacity split (Synergy, published Sept 2022) of ~53% Bloc A, ~15% Bloc B and ~32% elsewhere - i.e. on the broad hyperscale proxy the 'outside' share exceeded 20%, but this is general cloud capacity, not AI-specific >100 MW sites. In-phase Synergy releases flagged generative AI as driving much larger new facilities but gave no regional split. No dedicated series exists; proxy shown as background only.

items.summary: Latest regional split public during 2023: of hyperscale data-centre capacity, about 53% sat in Bloc A, 16% in a major third region, 15% in Bloc B and 16% elsewhere - roughly 32% outside the two leading jurisdictions on this broad (non-AI-specific) proxy.
items.detail: TelecomTV (Ray Le Maistre), 2022-09-12, reporting Synergy Research Group: Bloc A 53%, Europe 16%, Bloc B 15%, rest of world 16%; >800 hyperscale data centres. Pre-phase publication used as the latest available baseline during 2023.; proxy (regional share of hyperscale data-centre capacity; no dedicated series)
items.value: ~32% outside the two leading jurisdictions (hyperscale, all workloads)

items.summary: An industry tracker reported 926 major hyperscale data centres operating by mid-2023 with 427 more in the pipeline, and forecast total hyperscale capacity to almost triple in six years, with generative AI driving much larger, more power-dense facilities; no regional split given.
items.detail: Synergy Research Group, 'Hyperscale Data Center Capacity to Almost Triple in Next Six Years, Driven by AI', Reno NV, 2023-10-17.

items.summary: The same tracker estimated hyperscale operators held 37% of worldwide data-centre capacity (colocation 23%, on-premise 40%) as hyperscale sites approached 900; context for concentration, no regional split.
items.detail: Synergy Research Group, 'On-Premise Data Center Capacity Being Increasingly Dwarfed by Hyperscalers and Colocation Companies', 2023-07-12.

items.summary: No public 2023 dataset tracked announced >100 MW AI-specific data-centre capacity by jurisdiction; the named resolution sources (a dedicated AI data-centre tracker; IEA AI-energy analysis) post-date the phase.
items.detail: IEA data-centre page opened this run now shows only 2024-2026 material (Energy and AI reports), not usable under the as-of rule. Synergy's end-2023 split (Bloc A 51%) was published April 2024 - outside phase, excluded.
